summary_for_principal:
One kind of approval gate now actually works — the one where a person types in an answer (a date, a region, a number) rather than just saying yes or no.

This was previously refused outright: the shape was allowed in a definition but the system would crash confusingly the moment anyone tried to run one, so it was blocked at the door instead. It's now built for real, following the design from the last round.

Two smaller technical decisions were mine to make, both conservative: an automated or policy-based reviewer can still be asked first on this kind of gate, but can never actually supply the answer itself (nothing in this system today gives it a way to), so it's skipped over in favour of asking a person, without erroring. And a submitted answer is checked against its declared type (text, number, one of a fixed list, etc.) before being accepted, so a wrong-shaped answer is rejected rather than silently stored.

Full test suite: 432 passed (16 new). Lint, formatting and type checks all clean.

Numbered actions:
1. Nothing needs deciding — built, tested, ready to merge when CI is green.

filled_in.gap: WP-05's own design named A2 (a policy/agent decider on an INPUT gate always resolves INDETERMINATE-equivalent) but did not specify exactly how that decider's own PERMIT/DENY/INDETERMINATE verdict (from evaluate_policy_decider/check_agent_decision, both unchanged, both still returning ADR-028's Verdict) gets translated into an AnswerOutcome's own answered: bool.
filled_in.assumed: Always record answered=False for a policy/agent decider on an INPUT gate, regardless of what Verdict it actually returned — the underlying verdict is kept in the attempt's own output (policy_verdict/agent_verdict) for provenance, but never drives routing, since neither PolicyPort nor decision@1 has anywhere to carry a real typed answer. This is the conservative reading: a policy decider that happens to return PERMIT is not silently treated as if it had somehow answered.
filled_in.grounded_in: CLAUDE.md's 'do not invent a rule in code' — D26's own decision log already named this exact gap (no port/profile shape exists for a policy/agent decider to carry a typed value) as spec-silent; treating any of its existing Verdict values as an answer would be inventing meaning §7.6 does not state.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Low — a future pass that adds a real answer-carrying shape to PolicyPort/decision@1 can change this single translation point without touching resolve_input_gate's own sequencing logic.

filled_in.gap: decide()'s existing signature required verdict as a plain positional-shaped keyword argument; WP-05's design said 'value alongside (or instead of) a verdict' without specifying whether both could ever be given together, or what happens if the wrong one is given for a gate's own kind.
filled_in.assumed: Made verdict and value mutually exclusive and required-by-kind: an APPROVAL gate must get verdict and must not get value; an INPUT gate must get value and must not get verdict. Both wrong-shaped cases are refused outright (EngineRefusal, raised directly from decide() before ever calling _drive_scope — the same shape skip()'s own early checks already use), not silently accepted or silently ignored.
filled_in.grounded_in: CLAUDE.md's 'fail closed' and 'survive the bad-but-conformant attack' — a caller passing both, or the wrong one, is exactly the kind of malformed-but-plausible call this format's own principles ask to refuse rather than guess at.
filled_in.reversal_cost: None avoided — the refusal is a pure validation addition; nothing about the existing APPROVAL path's own required verdict changed.

decisions.headline: D41 — kind: INPUT gates (§7.6) are now implemented, closing D26: a person decider answers via a new decide(..., value=...) parameter; policy/agent deciders are asked but can never actually answer one, and always pass on.
decisions.problem: D26 refused every INPUT gate outright, at both validation and engine runtime, because §7.6's own one-sentence description left three questions genuinely open: which decider kinds may answer at all, what shape an agent decider's own answer takes, and what public call a person uses to submit one.
options_rejected: Invent a new PolicyPort method and a new/extended agent profile so all three decider kinds could genuinely answer an INPUT gate: rejected — unstated by §7.6, and a materially bigger port/profile change for a want nothing in the corpus or the 65 cataloged use cases actually asks for; every real INPUT gate use case reviewed wants a person's own typed answer.

Add a fourth answer() call to §12.1 instead of extending decide(): rejected — decide() already means 'a person resolves this gate's own open decision'; a separate call would duplicate decide()'s own replay/permission-check plumbing for no structural difference from a single new, kind-gated optional parameter.
decisions.cost_to_change: Low — AnswerOutcome/resolve_input_gate are additive alongside DeciderOutcome/resolve_gate; decide()'s new parameters are additive with a backwards-compatible default; every _advance_gate branch point is an if node.kind == "INPUT" alongside the existing APPROVAL path, not a replacement of it.
